original_statement: Membership epochs are real: adding a member re-keys forward; they cannot read earlier epochs. Removing a member rotates the epoch immediately. The UI seam depends on this.
restatement: The module core's membership keying scheme must make epochs real, not cosmetic: (s1) adding a member advances the key epoch, and the new member's derived key set is disjoint from every prior epoch's keys; (s2) across the full reachable membership/epoch state space, no member can decrypt content from any epoch before their join epoch; (s3) removing a member rotates the epoch immediately — content encrypted right after a removal is unreadable with the removed member's last-held key.

restatement_clauses.text: Adding a member advances the key epoch, and the new member's derived key set is disjoint from every prior epoch's keys.
Across the full reachable membership/epoch state space (any sequence of adds and removes), no member can decrypt content from any epoch before their join epoch.
Removing a member rotates the epoch immediately — content encrypted right after a removal is unreadable with the removed member's last-held key.

goal: A module-core keying scheme where adding a member advances the epoch and hands the new member only forward-facing key material, and removing a member rotates the epoch immediately — both enforced structurally, not by convention.

acceptance_tests.proves: A newly added member's derived key set never overlaps any epoch that predates their join — the forward-secrecy boundary is real at the moment of joining, not just eventually.
acceptance_tests.description: Adding a member advances the key epoch, and the new member's derived key set is disjoint from every prior epoch's keys.

acceptance_tests.proves: Every reachable (membership-set, epoch) state, reached by any sequence of adds and removes, is free of a pre-join-epoch decrypt leak — not just the single add/remove sequence a hand-written test happens to try.
acceptance_tests.description: Across the full reachable membership/epoch state space (any sequence of adds and removes), no member can decrypt content from any epoch before their join epoch.

acceptance_tests.proves: Epoch rotation on removal is immediate, not lazy or eventual — content encrypted in the very next step after a removal is already unreadable with the removed member's last key, across many random remove-then-encrypt trials.
acceptance_tests.description: Removing a member rotates the epoch immediately — content encrypted right after a removal is unreadable with the removed member's last-held key.
